neighbours.label: The verb 'tell' (Tell us / and tell them) in chatty informal prose; strong activations are otherwise a heterogeneous mix
fire: We loved the shaver so much that my brother and I decided to call the company and tell them how great it was.
Which of these desserts would you pick? Tell us in the comments below, and we may feature your favourite.
If you ever spot that old guy by the harbour, please come find me and tell me what he was fishing for.
Honestly the best part of the trip was the food, so go ahead and tell your friends to book early.
She grabbed the phone, ready to tell her mother everything about the strange noise in the attic.
Did the concert live up to the hype? Tell me what you thought, because I could not make it.
Nobody had the nerve to tell the coach that the bus had already left without us.
Another winner has been picked, and the editors will tell each finalist by email on Friday.
quiet: We loved the shaver so much that my brother and I decided to write the company a long thank-you note.
Which of these desserts would you pick? Vote in the comments below, and we may feature your favourite.
If you ever spot that old guy by the harbour, please wave at him and ask what he was fishing for.
Honestly the best part of the trip was the food, so go ahead and book early with your friends.
She grabbed the phone, ready to whisper her mother's name into the quiet of the attic.
Did the concert live up to the hype? Share what you thought, because I could not make it.
Nobody had the nerve to ask the coach whether the bus had already left without us.
Another winner has been picked, and the editors will email each finalist on Friday.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top examples are a scatter (' to' after 'excuse', ' tell', 'ed', CJK particles, punctuation) with no single token or context; the clearest repeated item is 'tell'. Census hints at foods/drinks but only 56% of foods in templates, so the label is a weak token hypothesis and partial coverage is expected.
